note: Geometry is a public GrabCAD surveillance hexacopter sample standing in for a real AXOM airframe, converted from IGES (the snapshot ships no STEP). IGES carries no part names at all, so every solid arrives as `part_N` and each rotor group below was resolved purely by XZ position against the six rotor centres — see docs/MEMORY.md. Solids whose function geometry does not make obvious are deliberately left unauthored rather than given an invented name. All `website` figures are illustrative placeholders, not specifications.

part_35#35.description: Forward lift rotor on the aircraft centreline. Six rotors let the aircraft stay controllable after a single rotor failure, which is why this class is used for payload work over people or property.

specs.label: Rotating / fixed

specs.note: Both blades are one watertight solid with no separable mesh island, so a rigid pitch is geometrically impossible here.

part_0#0.description: Lower half of the frame sandwich. All six booms are clamped between this plate and the upper plate.

part_37#37.description: Upper half of the frame sandwich, closing the boom clamps.

part_50#50.description: Tall starboard leg. The height exists to give the gimbal below the airframe clearance to rotate on the ground.

part_51#51.description: Tall port leg, mirroring the starboard side.

part_52#52.description: Raises the satellite navigation receiver clear of the airframe and its electrical noise.

part_53#53.description: Stabilised gimbal slung under the centre plate. It isolates the sensor from airframe attitude, so the aircraft can pitch into wind while the camera stays level.

part_54#54.description: Imaging payload carried in the gimbal cradle.
